## FX Index Dashboard – End of Round 5

The FX Index tracks how each currency is performing in the market.

::: {.callout-note}
Higher scores indicate relative strength and stability. Lower scores indicate pressure.
:::

| Country | FX Index | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Atlantica | 101.0 | Stable / softening |
| Noravia | 100.8 | Stable |
| Pacifica | 100.9 | Stable |
| Industralia | 100.4 | Stable / softening |
| Mercatoria | 100.1 | Softening |
| Petrovia | 100.0 | Stable / vulnerable |
| Agrona | 99.3 | Under pressure |
| Frontieria | 100.0 | Stable / fragile |

::: {.callout-important}
Currencies remain relatively stable, but stability is now being achieved alongside weakening economic conditions.
:::

## Trade & Alliance Tracker – End of Round 5

Trade agreements remain in place, but their ability to offset weakening global demand is diminishing.

| Agreement | Type | Countries | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Atlantica–Pacifica | Multilateral / Open | Atlantica, Pacifica | Supports stability but limited growth impact |
| Noravia Strategic Goods | Strategic Goods | Noravia, Industralia, Mercatoria | Helps supply chains but not enough to offset slowdown |
| Industralia–Mercatoria | Multilateral | Industralia, Mercatoria | Trade linkages important but demand is weakening |
| Petrovia–Agrona | Strategic Goods | Petrovia, Agrona | Still valuable but commodity demand is falling |

::: {.callout-note}
Trade agreements now matter most for **preserving demand**, not expanding it.
:::

---

## Interpretation for Students

- FX stability ≠ economic strength  
- Global tightening → lower demand → weaker growth  
- Trade helps cushion the fall, but cannot fully prevent slowdown  

::: {.callout-important}
You are now entering a **recession scenario**. Your decisions must balance recovery and credibility.
:::
